sentences.text: How to pack a lunch for school.
Kids, would you like to learn how to pack your own lunch for school?
Sure. Can we pack whatever we want?
Well, almost. We need to choose food that's healthy, filling, and easy to carry.
Let's start with the main meal.
What should we put in our lunch boxes?
Can I have a ham and cheese sandwich?
Yes, of course.
Okay. What's the first step?
Take two slices of bread and spread a little butter on one side of each slice.
Like this.
That's right.
Now put a slice of ham on the bread.
Then add a slice of cheese and some lettuce.
Now place the other slice of bread on top.
Done. Should I cut it in half?
Yes, you can cut it diagonally to make two triangles.
Look, my sandwich looks just like the ones in the cafe.
It looks delicious.
Mom, I'd like to make a chicken wrap.
Great choice. A chicken wrap is easy to make and perfect for a school lunch.
What do I need?
First, take a tortilla and put a small handful of chicken in your wrap.
Spread it down the middle of the tortilla.
Add some lettuce, a few cucumber slices, and some grated cheese.
Can I add a little sauce, too?
Sure. A little yogurt sauce would go nicely with the chicken.
This looks really good, but how do I wrap it without everything falling out?
Fold the two sides in first, then roll it up tightly from the bottom.
Well done, sweetheart.
Now, let's put everything into your lunch boxes.
Can I take an apple and some crackers?
Of course. And don't forget your water bottle.
I'll take some grapes and a small yogurt. Perfect.
We made our own lunches.
I'm proud of you both.
The more you practice, the easier it gets.
How to change a light bulb.
Dad, what are you doing?
I'm changing the light bulb.
It stopped working yesterday.
Can I help you?
Sure, but first I need to turn off the power at the circuit breaker.
Can't you just switch off the light?
That's not enough.
We need to make sure there's no electricity going to the light fixture.
What do you do next?
Now, I'll carefully unscrew the old bulb.
Do you turn it to the left?
That's right.
You turn it counterclockwise to loosen it.
And then you put the new one in.
Exactly. But we need to make sure it's the right type and size.
How do you know which bulb to buy?
We check the label on the old bulb.
This one is an LED bulb and it uses 9 W.
What's the difference between an LED bulb and a regular one?
LED bulbs use less electricity and usually last much longer.
That's good. So, can I screw in the new one?
No, I'll handle the installation.
Electrical work should always be done by an adult.
Okay. What's next?
I'll carefully screw the new bulb into the light fixture.
And now we turn the power back on.
Yes. I'll switch the circuit breaker back on and test the light.
Turn on the light.
It works. The room is bright again.
Great. And remember, never try to change a light bulb yourself when you're home alone.
I won't, Dad.
How to sew a button.
Mom, look. A button fell off my favorite shirt.
Oh no. Don't worry.
We can sew it back on.
Can you do it for me?
I can, but how about I teach you?
It's a useful skill to have.
Really? Is it difficult?
Not at all.
You just need a needle and some thread.
Okay. What do we do first?
First, we need to thread the needle.
Take a piece of thread and pass it through the eye of the needle.
This tiny hole, it's so small.
I know. Try twisting the end of the thread to make it easier.
Oh, I got it.
Great job.
Now, tie a knot at the end so the thread won't slip through the fabric.
Okay, what's next?
Place the button where it belongs.
Hold it in place with one hand while you carefully push the needle through one of the holes.
Like this. That's right.
Should I do it again?
Yes. Repeat the process a few times.
I think I'm almost done. You are.
Now make a small knot on the back of the fabric to secure the thread.
And then I cut the thread.
Exactly. Use the scissors carefully and cut off the extra thread.
Look, Mom. I did it all by myself.
You did a wonderful job.
Now you know how to sew a button.
I do. Maybe I can fix your shirt. Next.
Grandma comes to visit.
Grandma, you're here.
Hello, my dear.
Oh, come here and give me a hug.
We missed you so much.
I missed you, too.
Mom, it's so lovely to see you.
Oh, sweetheart. It's wonderful to see you, too.
Come on in.
We've been looking forward to your visit.
Thank you, dear.
So, how are you all settling into your new home?
Great. We love it here.
We want to show you around, Grandma.
I'd love that.
I'd love to show you around, too, Mom, but I need to finish preparing the cookies.
Make yourself at home.
Don't worry, dear.
You go ahead.
I'll have a look around with the children.
Let's start with the living room.
Oh, what a lovely room.
It's so bright and spacious.
This is our favorite room.
We watch movies here.
And I love this big window.
You get so much sunlight.
Come and see the kitchen, Grandma.
It's right over here.
Oh, there you are.
I'm just getting the cookies ready.
What do you think of our kitchen, Mom?
Oh, it's beautiful.
I like the wooden cabinets and the big kitchen island.
Now, let's show you our rooms.
Oh, I'd love to see them.
This is my bedroom.
I have a desk by the window so I can do my homework here.
What a lovely little space.
And look at all those books.
I put them on those shelves myself.
Well done. And where's your room, Oliver?
Right across the hall. Come on.
Oh, I see.
Your rooms are right next to each other.
Yes. And look, I have a new gaming quarter.
That's nice. But I hope you don't spend all day playing games.
Don't worry, Grandma.
I still have plenty of time for other things.
Grandma, we also have a small garden at the back of the house.
Really? Can we go and have a look?
Sure.
There's a little patio, too.
We eat outside when the weather is nice.
How lovely. I can already imagine us having lunch together out here.
Everyone, tea and cookies are ready.
That smells wonderful.
Come on, Grandma.
Let's go back inside.
Thank you for showing me around, children.
Your new home is lovely.
Who's doing the chores today?
All right, everyone.
We need to do some housework today.
The house is getting a little messy.
What do we have to do?
Well, the kitchen needs cleaning.
The dishes need putting away.
And the living room needs tidying up.
We also need to take out the trash and vacuum the floors.
Do we have to do all that today?
Yes, sweetheart. If we all help, it won't take very long.
Okay, I'll help.
How about we divide the chores fairly?
I'll vacuum the floors and take out the trash. Great.
I'll clean the kitchen and wipe down the counters.
What about me?
I'd like you to dust the furniture in the living room and arrange the books on the shelves.
Sure. I'll make everything look nice and neat.
And what am I supposed to do?
You're in charge of loading the dishwasher.
Oh, come on.
Why do I always get the worst job?
It's a simple job.
Just put the dirty dishes in the dishwasher.
What about the glasses and cups?
Put them on the top rack.
All right, I think I can handle that.
Then I'll come and start the dishwasher.
If we finish early, can we order pizza tonight?
Yes, pizza sounds great.
That's a good idea.
If everyone does their part, we can have pizza for dinner.
Deal. Now, let's get to work.
There's no hot water.
James, there's no hot water.
I just turned on the shower and the water is freezing.
Really? That's strange.
We had hot water this morning.
Maybe something's wrong with the water heater.
But I also wanted to take a nice hot bath tonight.
Me, too. It's Saturday evening.
All right, don't panic.
Let me have a look.
Do you know how to fix it?
I'll see what I can find.
First, let's check the control panel.
What's that symbol on the screen?
Oh, look. It's set to holiday mode.
What does that mean?
It means the water heater uses very little energy while we're away.
It doesn't keep the water hot as usual.
Maybe someone pressed the wrong button.
That's probably what happened.
Let me switch it back to normal mode.
There, it's back to normal mode and the heater is starting to warm up the water.
Is that all?
I think so.
So, we can take hot showers or baths again.
Not just yet.
We need to give it some time to heat the water.
How long? Maybe an hour or so.
Well, at least we don't have to call anyone.
Exactly. Sometimes the problem is simpler than it looks.
Thanks for watching and be sure to subscribe to our YouTube channel for more videos like this.
